cells.gaps: The one row describes the flow of birth and death notifications only, from health offices on paper to electronic processing at district level; nothing shows clinics' routine reports of patients treated entering the system, and the latest year the source cites is 2011. No tier, clinic share, governance or twelve-month fact has been found.
cells.note: A national health information system keyed at district level is on record, with a health-office pilot in some governorates, which meets stage 2. Stage 3 needs the district system to take the clinics' routine reports, and the evidence shows only vital-event notifications.

cells.gaps: The Egypt Healthcare Authority's count of 265 primary care centres and units running its health information system (July 2026, EGY-015) covers the six first-phase Universal Health Insurance governorates only and gives no denominator; it postdates the compact's early pilots of December 2025 (EGY-006), so the newer stands. Records shared across governorates (November 2026, EGY-016) reach only the insurance system's governorates. No national share of primary clinics. The advancing flag rests on a proposal discussed in September 2026, with no timetable.
cells.note: Electronic records run in 265 primary care centres and units across six governorates (July 2026), primary clinics in some districts, which meets stage 3. Stage 4 needs more than half of primary clinics nationally on records retrievable at another facility, and nothing shows that.
